And he spoke with Jacob and said, "I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac; the land on which you sleep, to you I will give it, and to your seed after you.

And your seed shall be like the sand of the earth, and it shall spread abroad to the sea and to the east and to the north and to the south; and in you and in your seed all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed.
And behold—
—of your womb, or have I forsaken you?"
And when Rachel saw that Leah had borne Jacob four sons—Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah—Rachel said to Jacob, "Go in to Bilhah my handmaid, and she will conceive and bear me a son."
And she gave Bilhah her handmaid as a wife; and she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Dan, in the ninth month of this sixth year of the week.

And Jacob went in again to Bilhah, and she conceived and bore a second son to Jacob; and Rachel called his name Naphtali, in the fifth month of the seventh year, in the second year of the fourth week.

And Leah, seeing that she was restrained and was not bearing, gave her other handmaid to Jacob as a wife; and she conceived and bore a son, and Leah called his name Gad, in the twelfth month of the eighth year, on the third day of the fifth week.
He went in to her, and she bore him a son, and she called his name Asher, in the second month on the tenth day, in the fifth year of the fourth week.
He went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Issachar; and in the fourth year, in the month of the fifth year, on the day of the fourth week, she gave him to a nurse.

And Jacob went in again to Leah, and she conceived and bore two, a male and a female; and she called the name of the male Zebulun, and the name of the female Dinah, in the seventh month of the seventh year, the sixth of the fourth week.
God had mercy on Rachel and opened her womb, and she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the first day of the fourth month in the sixth year of this fourth week.

At the time when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wives and my sons, and I will go to my father Isaac and make a household for myself; for I have completed the years in which I served you for your two daughters, and I will go to the house of my father."
And Laban said to Jacob, "Stay with me for wages, and pasture my sheep again, and I will give you wages."
And they agreed concerning wages, that he should give him—
...that the name of that place was called 'Heap of Witness' according to this hill.

For previously the land of Gilead was called the land of the Rephaim, because it is the land of the Rephaim. And there were born the Rephaim, that is, giants of ten cubits, and nine, and eight cubits, and even seven cubits was their height.
And their dwelling was from the land of the children of Ammon as far as Mount Hermon, and the seats of their kingdom were Karnaim, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, and Misam, ... and Sihon.

And the Lord destroyed them because of the evil of their deeds, for they were exceedingly wicked; and in their place He caused the Amorites to dwell, wicked and sinful, such as no nation is hated, because they fulfilled all their sins; and they no longer have length of days upon the earth.
And Jacob sent Laban away, and he went into Mesopotamia, into the land of the east; and Jacob turned to the land of Gilead.

And in the ninth month Jacob crossed over with his eleven sons; and on that day his brother Esau came to him and was reconciled, and he went away from him to the land of Seir, and Jacob dwelt in tents.
And in the first year of this jubilee, in the fifth week, he crossed the Jordan and dwelt across the Jordan. And he was pasturing his sheep from the Salt Sea as far as the Ascent of Akrabbim.
And he sent to his father Isaac from all his possessions garments, and food, and meat, and drink, milk, butter, and cheese, and dates from the valley.

And to his mother Rebekah each year four times, between the seasons of the months: between the threshing floor and the autumn harvest, and between autumn and the rains, and between the rains and the spring, to this tower of Abraham.
For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and gone up to the tower of his father Abraham, and dwelt there in his land, he and his sons.

Because at the time when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took for himself a wife, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, and he took all the flocks of his father and his wives, and going up, he dwelt in Mount Seir and left his father Isaac at the Well of the Oath.
Therefore Isaac went up from the Well of the Oath to the tower of his father Abraham in the mountain of Hebron.

There Jacob was sending whatever was needed to his father and to his mother season by season, all things that were necessary for all their needs; and they blessed Jacob with all their heart and with all their soul.
And in the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.

And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land; and he defiled her, for he lay with her, and she was a young girl, twelve years old.

And afterward he asked for her from her father and all her brothers as a wife. And Jacob and his sons were indignant with the men of Shechem because they had defiled their sister Dinah; and they spoke to them deceitfully and mocked them with craftiness.

...Simeon and Levi; and Simeon and Levi resolved in their heart to destroy them, and they executed judgment upon the men of Shechem... whom they found in it, and they did not leave in it even one, for they killed all of them in judgment, because they had defiled Dinah their sister.

...it shall not be any longer that the daughters of Israel are defiled; because judgment was decreed in heaven against them, that they should fight with the sword against all of Shechem, because they wrought shame in Israel.

And the Lord delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob, that they might uproot them with the sword and that judgment might be executed upon them; and it shall no longer be in... Israel that a virgin of Israel be defiled.

And whatever man there is from the children of Israel who sees fit to give his daughter or his sister to any man from the seed of the Gentiles shall perish and be stoned with stones, because he has wrought shame in Israel; and the woman shall be burned with fire, because she has contaminated the house of her father; he shall be uprooted from Israel.
And there shall be no harlot or abomination in Israel all the days of the generations of the earth, because Israel is holy to the Lord, and every man who defiles it shall die by stoning.
For thus it is written and decreed on the heavenly tablets concerning all the seed of Israel: that whoever defiles it shall surely die, and shall be stoned with stones.

And to this law there shall be no end of time, and for it there shall be no remission or any atonement; but rather let the man be cut off whoever defiles his daughter among the people of Israel, because from his seed he has given to a foreigner, and they acted impiously to contaminate it.

And you, Moses, command the children of Israel and testify to them that they must not give of their daughters to the Gentiles, and that they must not take for their sons from their daughters, for it is an abomination before the Lord.

For this reason I have written for you in the words of the law all the accounts of the deeds of the Shechemites which they did to Dinah, and how the sons of Jacob spoke, saying: 'We will not give our daughter to a man who has a foreskin, for that would be a reproach to us.'
And it is a reproach to Israel, those who give or take from the daughters of the Gentiles, because it is an abomination and uncleanness in all Israel.
And Israel shall not be cleansed from this abomination if he has a wife from the Gentiles, and it shall not be cleansed if we give of our daughters to any of the Gentiles.

For it is plague upon plague and curse upon curse, and all the judgments of plagues and the curse of curses will come upon anyone who does this deed; and if he transgresses and despises it, doing abominations and defiling the sanctuary of God, and for those who profane His holy name, the whole people together will be judged for all of his abominations.
And He will not show partiality, nor will He accept sacrifice or burnt offerings, nor will He smell a sweet aroma to receive it, concerning every man or woman in Israel who defiles the holy things.

Wherefore I commanded you, saying: 'Testify with this testimony in Israel, and see what was done to the Shechemites and to their sons, how they were delivered into the hand of the men, the sons of Jacob, and they killed them in judgment, and it was reckoned to them in truth and recorded for them as righteousness.'

And the seed of Levi was designated for the priesthood and as Levites, to serve before the Lord just as we do all the days; and Levi and his sons are blessed forever, because he was zealous for truth to execute judgment and vengeance upon all who rose up against Israel.
And thus blessing and righteousness are recorded for him as a testimony on the heavenly tablets before the God of all.

And the righteousness that a man does in his life will be remembered; through all the seasons of the year, up to a thousand years, it will be presented, and it will come to him and to his seed after him, and he is recorded as a righteous friend on the heavenly tablets.

I have written for you all these words and commanded you to proclaim them to the children of Israel, that they may not do evil, nor transgress the commandments, nor break the covenant ordained for them, but perform them; and they will be recorded as friends of God.

If, however, they transgress the covenant and act abominably in any of the ways written on the heavenly tablets, they shall be enemies of God, and they will be blotted out from the book of life and written in the book of destruction, among those who are uprooted from the earth.
And on the day when the sons of Jacob struck Shechem, a writing went up for them in heaven that they had executed truth and judgment and vengeance upon them; and they were recorded for a blessing.

And they brought Dinah their sister out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem: their sheep, and their cattle, and their donkeys, and all their substance, and all their herds; and they brought everything to Jacob their father.
And he spoke to them regarding why they had destroyed the city, for he feared those who inhabit the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
And the fear of the Lord came upon all the cities that were around Shechem, and they did not pursue after Jacob to harm him, because fear had fallen upon them.
And on the first day of the month ---.
--- son, for they are like you.
And he declared to him, saying: "In truth they are my sons, and you have truly seen, father, that they are my sons."
And they drew near to him, and turning, he kissed them and embraced them both together.
And the spirit of prophecy came into the mouth of Isaac, and he held Levi with his right hand and Judah with his left.
And he turned to Levi first and began to bless him first, and he blessed Levi, saying: "May the God of all and the Lord of the ages himself bless you and your sons for all ages.

And may the Lord grant to you and to your great seed to understand his glory, and he will draw your seed near to himself from all flesh so that you may serve him in his sanctuary like the angels of the presence and like the holy ones; and according to them shall the seed of your sons also be, for glory and greatness and sanctification; and he has sanctified them for all ages.

And they shall be princes and judges for all the seed of Jacob. They shall declare the word of God in truth, and they shall examine all his judgments in righteousness, and they shall declare my ways to this Jacob and my paths to this Israel. The blessing of God shall be given to his seed, that they may bless all the beloved seed.

Your mother called your name Levi, and in truth she called your name: you shall be for the beauty of God and a companion of all the sons of Jacob. Your table shall be for you, and you and your sons shall eat from it; and for all ages your table shall be full, and your food shall not fail for all ages.

And all who hate you shall fall before your face, and all your enemies shall be destroyed and perish. For he who blesses you shall be blessed, and if there is any nation that curses you, it shall be cursed."

And to Judah he said: "May God give you strength and power, that you may trample all who hate you. A prince shall you be, and one of your sons --- shall go forth and possess all the earth and the regions. Then the peoples will fear before your face, and all the nations will be dismayed, and all ---"
--- creating all things, to whom you prayed a prayer.
And he said to Rebekah: "Go with your son." And Rebekah went with her son Jacob, and Deborah her nurse with her, and they arrived at Bethel.
And he remembered the blessing with which his father had blessed him and his two sons, Levi and Judah; and he rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac:

"Now I know that I have eternal hope, and my sons, before Almighty God; and thus it was ordained concerning the two and their portion in the testimonies of eternity on the heavenly tablets, just as Isaac blessed them."
And they slept that night in Bethel, and Levi dreamed as though he were ordained as priest of the Most High God forever; and waking from his sleep, he blessed God.

And Jacob, rising early at dawn on the fourteenth day of this month, tithed everything that had come with him, from human being down to every living creature, and from gold down to every vessel and garment; he tithed everything.

And at that time Rachel was pregnant with her son Benjamin. Jacob counted his sons starting from him, and the lot went up and Levi fell as the portion of God; and his father clothed him in priestly garments and ordained him.

On the fifteenth day of this month he also offered upon the altar fourteen calves from the herd, and twenty-eight rams, and forty-nine sheep, and seven kids, and twenty-one male goats—these burnt offerings upon the altar of fruits, acceptable as a pleasing aroma before God.
This was his offering from the vow which he had vowed to tithe, along with their sacrifices and with their wine.

And when the fire consumed the frankincense upon the fire from above, he also offered as a peace offering two calves, four rams, two yearling lambs, and two male goats. And he did these once daily for seven days.
And he blessed and sang a hymn to God, who had delivered him from all his tribulations, and because he had fulfilled his vow.
And he tithed all ---
wherever they shall set the sole of their feet against the children of men.

And I will give to your seed all the blessings that are under heaven, and they shall rule and exercise authority over all nations according to their will, and after this they shall possess the whole earth and inherit it forever."
And when he finished speaking with him, he ascended from him; and Jacob was watching until he had ascended from him into heaven.

And he saw in a vision of the night, and behold, an angel of God was descending from heaven, and seven boxwood tablets were in his hand; and he gave them to Jacob, and he read and understood what was written on them, and what would come upon him and upon his sons for all ages.

And he showed him whatever was written on the boxwood tablets, and said to him: "Do not build up this place, and do not make it an eternal sanctuary, and do not dwell in this place, for this place shall not be so. But go to the place of the tower of Abraham your father, and live with Isaac your father until the day of your father's death.
For in Egypt you will die in peace, and in this land you will be buried in glory, and you will be laid in the tomb of your fathers with Abraham and Isaac.
Do not fear, for just as you have seen and read, so shall all things that are written come to pass."
And Jacob said: "Lord, how will I remember all that I have read and seen?" And he said to him: "I will remind you of everything."
And he ascended from him; and he awoke from his sleep and remembered everything that he had read and seen; and he kept secret all the words that he had read and seen.

And he observed one day there and sacrificed on it as much as he had been sacrificing on the previous days; and he called its name 'Retention', because he was retained there for one day, and the previous days he called feast days.
And thus it was revealed that they should be done, and it was written on the heavenly tablets; on account of which it was revealed to him to observe that day and to add it to the seven feast days.
And its name was called 'Retention', because it was added to the days of the feast days according to the number of the days of the year.

And on the twenty-third day of this month, during the night, Deborah, the nurse of Rebecca, died. And they buried her below the city, under the oak near the brook; and they called the name of that place 'the Brook of Deborah'.
And Jacob went and returned to the Tower to his father Isaac; and Jacob sent in his hand rams and sheep and he-goats to make food for his father according to his desire.
And he went after his mother until he came to Ephrathah, and he remained there.
And Rachel gave birth to a boy on that night, and called his name Benjamin, in this jubilee, on the tenth day of the eighth month, in the first year of the sixth week.
Then Rachel died there, and she was buried in the land of Ephrath—that is, Bethlehem; and Jacob built a pillar over the tomb of Rachel on the way to her tomb.
And Jacob went and settled south of Migdal-Eder; and he went to his father Isaac, he and his wife Leah, on the first day of the tenth month.
And Reuben saw Bilhah, the handmaid of Rachel, the concubine of his father, bathing herself in water in a secret place, and he loved her.
And he went in secretly by night to Bilhah and found her sleeping in her bed alone in her tent.
And he slept with her, and she awoke; and behold, Reuben was with her on the bed. And lifting the coverlet, she seized him and cried out, and she recognized that it was Reuben.
And he was ashamed before her, and she released her hands from him, and he fled.
And she grieved exceedingly over this, and told everyone how he had come.

And when Jacob came, she reported it to him and said to Jacob: 'I am not clean for you, for I have been defiled toward you, because Reuben has defiled me and slept with me by night; and I was asleep and did not know until he uncovered my covering and slept with me.'
And Jacob was exceedingly angry with Reuben because he had slept with Bilhah.
And he did not know [her again...].
[... to show] partiality and [accept] gifts.

And make known to them the words of this covenant, so that they may hear and take heed concerning them, that they may not perish and may not be uprooted from the land; because there is uncleanness and abomination and hatred and defilement for all who do them on the earth in the sight of our God.

And it is a great sin upon the earth, because Israel is a holy people to the Lord their God, and a people of inheritance, and a priestly and royal people, and of sanctification; and there shall be no uncleanness in the midst of the holy people.
And in the third year of this sixth week Jacob and all his sons went and dwelt in the Tower of Abraham, beside his father Isaac and his mother Rebecca.

Now these are the names of the sons of Jacob: the firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun—the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah: Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah: Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, the only daughter of Jacob.

And when these arrived, they bowed down to Isaac and Rebecca. And when they saw them, they blessed Jacob and all his sons. And Isaac rejoiced exceedingly because he saw the sons of Jacob, his younger son, and he blessed them.
And in the forty-fourth jubilee, in the sixth year of this week, Jacob sent his sons to pasture his sheep, and his servants with them, to the plain of Shechem.
And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled against them and took up position in an ambush to kill them and to plunder their sheep [...].

Now Jacob and Levi and Judah and Joseph were in the Tower beside his father Isaac, because his spirit was faint and they could not leave him. And Benjamin was the youngest; for this reason he had remained with his father.

And the kings arrived: the king of Sappho, and the king of Arco, and the king of Saragan, and the king of Silo, and the king of Gaas, and the king of Beth-horon, and the king of Manesacer, and all who inhabit the hill country and who inhabit places in the land of Canaan.
And it was told to Jacob: 'Behold, the kings of the Amor[ites...].'
[...] until this day, and all my deeds and everything that is in my heart, that all my days I [...] to do good [...] to all.
And how could I not do this word which you command me, to do for my father and my brothers?
But I ask, tell me, mother, what perverse thing you have seen in me, so that I may turn away from it and the mercy of the Lord may be upon me.

And Rebecca said to him: 'My son, all my days I have not seen in you any perverse deed, but uprightness. And yet I will tell you the whole truth, my son: I am dying this year, and I shall not pass beyond this year further in my life. I am dying and shall live no longer; [...] fifty years am I completing in my life.'

And Jacob laughed at the words of his mother because [... she was to die]. And she was sitting before him and was strong, and not weak in her strength; for she was going out and coming in, and her teeth were strong, and sickness had not afflicted her all her days.
And Jacob said to her: 'Blessed am I if my days should approach the days of your life [...]. [...] in me [...] likewise [...] you have spoken with me concerning your death.'

And she went in [...] to Isaac and said to him: "One petition I ask of you, that you put Esau under an oath that he will not afflict his brother Jacob, nor persecute him, nor harbor enmity against him. For you know the mind of Esau, that it has been evil from his youth, and there is nothing upright in him. [...] his brother."
[...] all that he has done [...] day [...] until this day on which [...] seized [...].
We were asking [...] from him of our own things [...] as though he were showing mercy to us.
And he was bitter toward you because you blessed Jacob your son, who is perfect and truthful, for there is no malice in him [...].
And he served God with all his heart and with all his soul, and according to the visible commandments, according to the division of the times of his generations.
And in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the fourth year of the second week, Leah the wife of Jacob died, and they buried her in the double cave beside Rebecca his mother.
And all his sons and his servants were present to weep with him for Leah his wife, and to comfort him concerning her, for he was mourning for her.

For he loved her greatly from the day that Rachel her sister died, because she was perfect and upright in all her ways, and honored Jacob all the days that he lived with her, and he did not hear any wicked word from her mouth, because she was quiet and peaceful and [...] honorable [...].
And he remembered all her deeds which she did in her life, and therefore he loved her greatly with all his heart and with his soul.
And on the day Isaac, the father of Jacob and Esau, died, the sons of Esau heard that Isaac had given the greater [...] honorable portion to Jacob, his younger son, and they were very indignant.
And they disputed with Esau, saying: "Why has Jacob been set over you, though he is younger, and your father gave him the greater portion and made you inferior?"

And Esau said to them: "Because I gave the birthright to Jacob for a little boiled lentils; and on the day when my father sent me to hunt game for him so that he might eat and bless me, he came with deceit and brought food and drink to my father, and my father blessed him and placed me under his hand."

And now our father put us under an oath, me and him, that we should not seek evil against each other, each against his brother, and that we should be in love and in peace, each man with his brother, so that we do not practice malice against one another.

And they said to him: "We will not listen to you to make peace with him, because our strength is mightier than his strength, and we are stronger men than he. We will go against him, and kill him, and destroy him and [his] sons [...]."
[...] that we may give him glory.
Then Jacob bent his bow and sent forth an arrow and struck Esau his brother upon his right breast and struck him down.
And he shot a second arrow and struck Adoram the Aramaean near his left breast, and cast him down and killed him.
And after this the sons of Jacob went forth, they and their servants, divided toward the four winds of the tower.
And Judah went out first, and Naphtali and Gad with him, and fifty servants with him toward the south of the tower; and they slew whomever they found before them, and not even one of them escaped.
And Levi and Dan and Asher went out toward the east of the tower, and fifty with them, and they slew the warriors of Moab and Ammon.
Reuben and Issachar and Zebulun went out, and their fifty with them, and they also slew the warriors of the Philistines.

And Simeon and Benjamin and Hanoch the son of Reuben went out toward the west of the tower, and their fifty with them; and they slew four hundred fighting men of Edom and of the Horites; and six hundred and four sons of Esau fled with them, and they left the body of their father cast out upon the height which is in Adoraim.
And the sons of Jacob pursued after them as far as Mount Seir. And Jacob buried Esau his brother on the height which is Adoraim, and he returned into the tower.
And the sons of Jacob besieged the sons of Esau in Mount Seir, and subjugated them so that they became servants to the sons of Jacob.
And they sent to Jacob their father asking if they might make peace with them.
And they placed the yoke of fear upon them, that they should pay tribute to Jacob and to his sons all the days.
And they were paying tribute to Jacob until the day of his going down into Egypt.
And the children of Edom have not ceased from the yoke of fear which the sons of Jacob imposed on them until this day.
And these are the kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned over the children of Israel, until this day in the land of Edom:
Barad the son of Beor, and the name of his city was [...].

And she assailed him and took hold of him inside the house, that she might force him and sleep with her; and she closed the doors of the house and held him. But Joseph left his garments, and opening the door, fled outside from her presence.

And when the woman saw that he had spurned her, she lied to her husband against him before his master, saying: "This Hebrew servant of yours, whom you loved, attempted to force me, that he might sleep with me. And it happened when I raised my voice, he fled outside and left his garments in my hands, with which I had held his garments from below [...]."
And the Egyptian saw the garments of Joseph and the broken door, and heard the words of his wife, and put Joseph into the house of the bound, in the place where the king's prisoners were kept.

And he was there in bonds; and the Lord gave him favor in the sight of the chief of the prison, and mercy in his sight, because he saw that the Lord was with him, and everything that Joseph did, God made to prosper.

And therefore he gave everything into his hands. And the chief of the prison did not know anything of the things that were done in the prison, because Joseph was doing all of them, and the Lord made them prosper.

And he was there for two years. And at that time Pharaoh, king of Egypt, became angry with his two eunuchs, that is, with the chief cupbearer and with the chief baker, and he put them in prison in the house of the chief cook, in the prison-house in which Joseph also was held.
And the keeper of the prison appointed Joseph to serve them, and he served before them.
And the men dreamed dreams, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, and they told them to Joseph.
And just as Joseph had interpreted to them, so it happened to them: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had told him.

And the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph in the prison-house, though he had told him all that would happen to him; and he did not remember to intercede with King Pharaoh to release Joseph, for he forgot.

And at that time Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning the famine that was to come upon [...] the earth. And having awakened from sleep, he called all the interpreters of dreams who were in his kingdom and the enchanters, and he told them his dreams, but they could not interpret his dreams.
Then the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph and told King Pharaoh about him; and he brought him out of the prison-house and recounted in his presence the two dreams [...].
[...] interpreted [...]: 'The two dreams are one. There will be seven continuous years of abundance in all the land of Egypt, and seven years of famine; so it shall be in all the land.'

And now let Pharaoh appoint overseers over all the land of Egypt, who shall gather food throughout every city and store it up during the seven years of abundance as food for the seven years of famine that are to come, and the land will not perish from the famine, for it will be very severe over all the land.
And God gave Joseph favor and mercy in the sight of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants, 'Can we find a man more prudent and wiser than this one, since the Spirit of God is with him?'
And he placed him second to himself in all his kingdom and with authority over all the land of Egypt, and he set him upon the second chariot which belonged to Pharaoh.

And he clothed him with a garment of fine linen, and put a golden necklace around his neck, and they proclaimed before him, 'Elel and Habirel,' and he put a ring upon his hand. And he set him over all his house, and magnified him, and said, 'I shall not be greater than you except in my throne alone.'

And Joseph received authority over the whole land of Egypt. And all the princes of Pharaoh and his servants and all who did the king's work loved him, because he walked in truth, and there was in him no pride or arrogance [...].
[...] Tamar, his daughter-in-law: 'Remain as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up, and I will give you to him as a wife.'
And he grew up, but Bathshua, the wife of Judah, did not allow her son Shelah to take her. And Bathshua, the wife of Judah, died in the fifth year of this week.
And in the sixth year of this (week), Judah went up to shear his sheep in Timnasar; and it was told to Tamar, 'Behold, your father-in-law is going up to shear his sheep in Timnah.'
And she put off from herself the garments of her widowhood, and clothed herself in fine garments, and adorned herself, and sat at the gate by the road to Timnah.
And when Judah arrived, he found her and thought she was a harlot, and said to her, 'I will come in to you.' She said, 'Come in,' and he went in to her.
And she said to him, 'Give me my hire.' And he said, 'There is nothing in my hand except the ring that I have on my finger, and the necklace, and the staff that is in my hand.'
And she said to him, 'Give them to me until you send my hire.' And Judah said, 'I will send you a young goat.' And he gave them to her, and he was with her, and she conceived by him.
And Judah went to the sheep,

and he sent her a young goat by the hand of his Adullamite shepherd, but he did not find her. And he asked the men of that place, saying, 'Where is that harlot who was here?' And they said to him, 'There is no harlot here with us.'

And returning, he told Judah, saying, 'I did not find her, and moreover I asked the men of that place, and they said that there was no harlot in that place.' And Judah said, 'Let her keep them, lest perhaps she ridicule us.'
And when three months had passed for her, it became evident that she was with child; and they told Judah, saying, 'Behold, Tamar your daughter-in-law is with child.'
And Judah came to the house of her father and said to her father and to her brothers, 'Bring her out, and let her be burned with fire, because she has committed impurity in Israel.'

And it came to pass, when she was being brought out to be burned, that she sent to her father-in-law the ring, the necklace, and the staff, and said, 'Recognize whose these are; by him I am with child.'
Now in the land of Egypt there was bread, because Joseph had gathered the grain of the land during the seven years of abundance and had been guarding it.
And the Egyptians came to Joseph so that he might give them food; and opening the storehouses in which the grain was, he gave it to them to eat in the first year, for he sold it to them.

Now the famine grew very severe in the land of Canaan, and Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt; and he sent his ten sons to get food for themselves, but Benjamin he did not send with them. And the ten sons of Jacob arrived in Egypt.
And Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him; and Joseph spoke harshly to them and said to them, 'You have come to spy out the land,' and he imprisoned them.
And sending word, he summoned them, and taking Simeon from them, he bound him and sent his nine brothers away.
And he filled their containers and returned their money to them.
And he commanded them concerning their younger brother, that they should bring him.

And the sons of Jacob went up from the land of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, and they related to their father everything that had happened to them, and how harshly the ruler of the land had spoken with them, and had detained Simeon until we present our brother Benjamin to him.
And Jacob said: "You have bereaved me of my children. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more. If you take Benjamin, your malice will be accomplished against me."

And he said: "My son will not go with you, lest he fall ill on the way. For their mother bore these two; one has perished, and if you take this one and any illness befalls him on the way, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol."
For they told him that their money had also been returned to them in their sacks, and Jacob was afraid to send him with them.

Now the famine increased and grew severe in the land, for many of the children of the Egyptians had kept their seed in storage ever since they saw Joseph gathering grain and storing it in storehouses so that it might be preserved for the years of famine.
And the Egyptians ate them...
...the land of Egypt suffered because of the famine. And Joseph acquired the whole land of Egypt for Pharaoh for food, for he purchased the people, the beasts, and everything for Pharaoh.

And the seven years of famine came to an end, and Joseph gave seed and food to the people of the land so that they might sow the land in the eighth year, because the river had risen over all the land of Egypt.

For during the seven years of famine it had not risen and had not watered except a few places along the riverbank. And in the eighth year the Egyptians sowed their land and gathered good crops in that year.
This was the first year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

And Joseph took a fifth part of all that grew in the land of Egypt as a royal portion, and gave four parts to them for food and for seed; and Joseph established this as an ordinance for all the Egyptians throughout the whole land of Egypt unto this day.

And Israel lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and all the years of his life which he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years; and he expired and died in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the fourth year of the fifth week.
Israel blessed his sons before he died and told them whatever would happen to them in the land of Egypt in the last days. And he blessed them, and he blessed Joseph with a double portion in the land.
And he slept with his fathers and was buried in the double cave in the land of Canaan beside his father Abraham, in the tomb which he had dug for himself in Hebron.
And he gave all his books and the books of his fathers to his son Levi, that he might preserve them and renew them for his children unto this day.

And it came to pass after the death of Jacob that the children of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt and became a great nation; and they were of one heart, so that each one loved his brother, and brother joined with neighbor...
And the king of Canaan devised an evil plot to afflict them.

And at that time the Egyptians said: "Behold, the people of the children of Israel have multiplied greatly and have become more numerous than we. Come, therefore, let us afflict them before they multiply, and let us oppress them with their labors, lest war should confront us and then they also fight against us alongside our enemies, departing from our land, because their heart and their face are toward the land of Canaan."

And the king set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their labors. And they built fortified cities for Pharaoh—Pithom, Rameses, and On—and they rebuilt every wall that had fallen into ruin in the cities of Egypt.
And they reduced them to servitude with violence; and the more they oppressed them, the more they multiplied.
And the Egyptians abhorred the children of Israel.

And in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the seventh week, in its seventh year, his father came from the land of Canaan. And he begot in the fourth week, in its sixth year, of the forty-eighth jubilee. This is the time of tribulation upon the children of Israel.
And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a decree concerning them, that they should cast into the river all their male children who were born to them.
And they were watching for seven months until the time when you were born. And your mother hid you for three months, and they informed against her.

And being afraid, she made an ark and smeared it with bitumen and pitch, and placed it along the riverbank, and kept you in it for seven days. And your mother would come by night and nurse you with milk, and by day your sister Miriam guarded you from the birds.
And at that time Thermuthis, the daughter of Pharaoh, went out to bathe in the river, and she heard the sound of your crying, and she told her maiden to bring the child to her; and they brought you.
And taking you out of the ark, she had pity on you.
And your sister said to her: "Shall I go and call for you, if you wish, a Hebrew woman who may nurse him for you?" And she said to her: "Go."
And she called her mother and yours, Jochebed, and she gave wages to that woman...

...and taught... and when you completed... week, they brought you into the royal court. And you were... three weeks of years until the time when you went out from the royal court and saw an Egyptian beating your brother, and you struck him and dug in the earth and hid him in the sand.
And on the second day you found two of the children of Israel striving together, and you said to the one who was beating his neighbor: "Why are you beating your brother?"
And he was filled with wrath and indignation... and said: "Who made you a ruler or a judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" ...

And in the forty-ninth jubilee, in the sixth year of the third week, you departed and dwelt in the land of Midian... five weeks and one year. And in the fiftieth jubilee, in the second week, in its second year, you returned to Egypt.
And you yourself know who spoke with you under Mount Sinai, and what Prince Mastema wished to do with you when you were returning to Egypt on the way when you met him at the lodging place.
Did he not with all his power seek to kill you, that he might rescue the Egyptians from your hand, because he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and wreak vengeance on the Egyptians?
And I delivered you from his hand, and you performed the signs and wonders, whatever you were sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against all his people.

And God openly wrought a great defense for Israel, and struck them with blood, and with frogs, and gnats, and dog-flies, and with malignant sores which were ... and with the death of their livestock; and with hailstones he destroyed all their growing things, and the locust devoured what had been left from the hail; and with darkness, [and the death] of their firstborn, both of humans and of beasts; and upon all the gods of the Egyptians the Lord took vengeance...

...[all the] days of your life, that you may observe it every year, once a year, on its appointed days according to its law, and it shall not pass away. And it shall be on its appointed days, and from month to month.

For it is an eternal commandment, and written upon the heavenly tablets concerning all the children of Israel, that they should observe it every year on its day, once a year, throughout their generations; and there is no end of time for it, because it is ordained forever.

And the man who is clean and does not do it on the day of its appointed time, so as to bring an acceptable offering before the Lord, and to eat and to drink before the Lord on the day of his feast, shall be cut off; and the man [who is] clean and who is near, because he did not offer the offering to the Lord in its appointed season, that man shall bear his sin.

And the children of Israel shall come and observe the Passover at its appointed time, on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the evening, from its third part until the third part of the night; for two parts of the day are in light, and the third part is in the evening.
This is what the Lord commanded you, that you should observe it in the evening.

And no one shall sacrifice at any hour of daylight, but only in the evening, and they shall eat it during the evening hours until the third part of the night; and whatever remains of all the flesh after the third part of the night shall be burned with fire.

And it shall not be boiled in water, nor shall it be eaten raw, but roasted on fire you shall carefully eat it: its head with its entrails and with its feet you shall roast with fire. And no bone among all its bones shall be broken, and there shall be no affliction among the children of Israel on this day.

Therefore the Lord commanded the children of Israel to observe the Passover on the day of its appointed time, and no bone of it shall be broken, for it is a feast day and a day of commandment. It shall not pass from day to day, nor from month to month, but [shall be kept] at its appointed time.

And you, command the children of Israel to observe the Passover throughout their generations every year, once a year, on the day of its appointed time; and it shall be an acceptable testimony before God, and no plague shall come upon them from him to destroy or to cut them off in that year in which they observe the Passover at its appointed time according to all its commandments.
And it shall not be eaten outside the sanctuary of the Lord, but beside the tabernacle of the Lord; and the whole congregation of the children of Israel shall observe it at its appointed time.

And every man who neglects in the muster to eat it in the sanctuary of our God before the Lord, from twenty years old and upward—because it is thus commanded and written that it should be eaten in his sanctuary—

And when the children of Israel come into the land of their possession, into the land of Canaan, and they set up the tabernacle of God in the midst of the land in one of their tribes until the day on which the sanctuary of God is built in the land, they shall come and observe the Passover before the tabernacle of God every year.

And at the time when the house is built in the name of the Lord in the land of their possession, there they shall offer and slaughter the Passover in the evening toward the going down of the sun, in the third part of the day.

And they shall offer its blood upon the base of the altar, and they shall offer the fat upon the fire of the altar, and they shall eat the flesh roasted with fire in the court of the house sanctified in the name of the Lord.

And they shall not be permitted to observe the Passover in their cities in any place, except before the tabernacle of the Lord and before the house where his name has dwelt upon it; and they shall not go astray from following the Lord.

And you, Moses, command the children of Israel that they keep the ordinance of the Passover; and declare to them, as it was commanded to you, year by year at the time of its days, and concerning the festival of Unleavened Bread, that they should eat unleavened bread for seven days and celebrate its festival, and offer an offering day by day throughout the seven days of joy before...
Et il y habita deux ans. Puis il partit de là vers le sud jusqu’à Baaloth, et la famine survint sur le pays.
Et Abram se rendit en Égypte la troisième année de la semaine d’années, et il habita dans le pays d’Égypte pendant cinq ans avant que sa femme ne lui fût enlevée.
Et Tanis, ville d’Égypte, fut alors bâtie sept ans après Hébron.
Et il arriva, lorsque Pharaon eut enlevé Sara, femme d’Abram, que le Seigneur frappa Pharaon et sa maison de grands fléaux à cause de Sara, femme d’Abram.

Et Abram devint alors très illustre par ses grandes richesses en brebis, en bœufs, en ânes, en chameaux, en chevaux, en serviteurs, en servantes, en argent et en or en abondance ; Lot, le fils de son frère, possédait lui aussi des richesses.

Et Pharaon rendit Sara, femme d’Abram, à son mari et le renvoya de la terre d’Égypte ; et il parvint au lieu où il avait d’abord dressé sa tente, au lieu de l’autel, avec Aï à l’est et Béthel à l’ouest, et il bénit le Seigneur son Dieu qui l’avait ramené en paix.

Et il arriva, au quarante et unième jubilé, la troisième année de la première semaine d’années, qu’il revint en ce lieu, offrit des holocaustes et invoqua le nom du Seigneur : « Tu es le Dieu Très-Haut, mon Dieu pour les siècles des siècles ! »
Et la quatrième année de cette semaine d’années, Lot se sépara de lui et habita à Sodome. Et les gens de Sodome étaient de grands pécheurs et iniques dans leur cœur.
c’est pourquoi Lot, le fils de son frère, s'était séparé de lui, parce qu’il n’avait pas d’enfants.

Lot fut fait captif loin de lui. Or, la quatrième année de cette semaine de ce même jubilé, Dieu dit à Abram : « Lève les yeux depuis le lieu où tu te trouves, vers l’ouest, le sud, l’est et le nord ;

car toute la terre que tu vois, je te la donnerai, à toi et à ta descendance, pour toujours ; et je rendrai ta descendance comme le sable de la mer, si bien que ta descendance ne pourra être dénombrée.
Lève-toi donc, parcours-la dans sa longueur et sa largeur, et vois tout, car je la donnerai à ta descendance. » Et Abram partit pour Hébron et y habita.
lui, et je le multiplierai et l’accroîtrai grandement ; car il engendrera douze princes, et je ferai de lui une grande nation.
Mais mon alliance, je l’établirai avec Isaac, que Sara t’enfantera à cette même époque, l’année prochaine.
Et il acheva de parler avec lui, et Dieu s’éleva au-dessus d’Abraham.

Et Abraham fit comme Dieu le lui avait dit : il prit Ismaël, son fils, tous ceux qui étaient nés dans sa maison ainsi que ceux achetés à prix d'argent, tous les mâles de sa maison, et il circoncit la chair de leur prépuce en ce jour-là.
Et Abraham se circoncit en ce jour-là, ainsi que les gens nés dans sa maison, ses serviteurs domestiques et ceux achetés à prix d'argent, même d'entre les fils de l’étranger : il les circoncit tous.
Telle est la loi pour toutes les générations du monde, et il n’est pas permis de dépasser un seul de ces jours, car c’est une ordonnance éternelle, prescrite et inscrite sur les tables célestes,

afin que tout nouveau-né dont la chair du prépuce n’aura pas été circoncise au huitième jour n’appartienne point à l’alliance que Dieu a conclue avec Abraham ; car il appartient aux fils de la destruction, et il n'y a plus sur lui de signe attestant qu’il appartient à Dieu, mais bien à l’extermination et à la perdition hors de la terre, parce qu'il a rompu l'alliance du Seigneur notre Dieu.

Car tous les anges de la Face et tous les archanges de la bénédiction, depuis les jours de leur création en présence des anges de la Face et des anges de la sanctification, ont sanctifié Israël afin qu'il soit avec Lui et avec les anges de Ses saints.
Et toi, ordonne aux enfants d’Israël de garder l’alliance de ce signe dans toutes leurs générations comme une alliance éternelle, et ils ne seront point retranchés de la terre.
Car il a été décrété dans l’ordonnance de l’alliance qu’elle soit gardée à perpétuité pour tous les enfants d’Israël.

Car Dieu ne s'est pas attaché Ismaël, ses fils, ses frères et Ésaü, et ne les a pas choisis, bien qu’ils soient eux aussi de la descendance d’Abraham comme Il les a connus, mais c'est Israël qu’il a choisi pour être son peuple.
Et il l’a sanctifié et...
toutes leurs œuvres, combien ils étaient iniques, grands pécheurs et impurs, commettant des souillures dans leur propre chair et accomplissant des abominations sur la terre.
Car c'est ainsi que Dieu exercera son jugement dans tous les lieux où l'on commettra l’abomination de Sodome : ainsi les jugera-t-il.
Et nous avons délivré Lot de là, car Dieu s’est souvenu d’Abraham pour le faire échapper du milieu de la destruction.

En effet, lui et ses filles ont commis sur la terre une iniquité telle qu'il n'en avait pas été commis sur toute la terre depuis les jours d’Adam jusqu’à lui, à savoir qu'un homme couchât avec ses propres filles.

Voici en effet qu’il est ordonné et écrit sur les tables célestes concernant toute leur descendance que de tels individus soient ôtés et exterminés, et que leur jugement s’accomplisse selon le jugement de Sodome, de sorte qu’il ne subsiste d'eux aucune semence humaine sur la terre au jour du jugement.
Et en ce mois, Abraham partit d’Hébron, s'en alla et s’établit entre Cadès et Shour, dans les confins de Guérar.
Et au milieu du cinquième mois, il se déplaça de là et habita près du Puits du Serment.
Et au milieu du sixième mois, Dieu visita Sara et fit pour elle comme il l’avait dit.
Et elle conçut et mit au monde un fils au septième mois, au milieu du mois, au temps que Dieu avait fixé à Abraham ; c’est le jour de la fête des prémices qu’Isaac naquit.
Et Abraham circoncit son fils le huitième jour ; il fut le premier à être circoncis selon l’alliance établie à perpétuité.

Et la sixième année de cette quatrième semaine d’années, nous sommes apparus à Abraham près du Puits du Serment, et nous nous sommes montrés à lui comme nous l’avions dit à Sara, annonçant que nous reviendrions vers elle et qu’elle aurait conçu son fils.

Et nous revînmes au septième mois, et nous trouvâmes Sara enceinte sous nos yeux. Et nous le bénîmes et lui fîmes connaître tout ce qui avait été décrété à son sujet, comment il devait mourir, qu’il engendrerait encore six fils et qu’il les verrait tous avant de mourir ; mais c'est en Isaac que sa postérité sera multipliée et que son nom sera perpétué.

Et toute la postérité de ses fils deviendra des nations et sera comptée parmi les nations, mais parmi les fils d’Isaac, il en sera un qui formera une descendance sainte et ne sera point compté parmi les nations,

car il appartiendra au lot du Très-Haut, puisque toute sa postérité est échue en possession à Dieu pour être à Dieu un peuple sanctifié d'entre toutes ses nations, afin d’être un royaume de prêtres et un peuple saint.
Puis nous reprîmes notre chemin, et nous rapportâmes à Sara tout ce que nous lui avions annoncé ; et ils se réjouirent tous deux d’une grande joie.
Et il bâtit là un autel au Seigneur qui l’avait délivré et qui lui avait fait grâce dans le pays de son séjour ; et il célébra en ce mois une fête de joie pendant sept jours auprès de l’autel,
et il dressa des tentes pour lui et pour ses serviteurs lors de ce jour de fête. Et il fut le premier à célébrer la fête des Tentes sur la terre.

Et durant ces jours, il offrait chaque jour sur l’autel en offrande au Seigneur deux veaux, deux béliers, sept brebis et un bouc pour le péché, afin de faire propitiation par lui pour lui-même et pour sa descendance.

Et en sacrifice de paix : sept béliers, sept chevreaux, sept brebis et sept boucs, avec leurs oblations et leurs libations de vin ; et il brûlait toute leur graisse sur l’autel en sacrifice de bonne odeur.

Et matin et soir, il faisait brûler un encens composé d’oliban, de galbanum, de stacté, de nard, de myrrhe, de nard indien et de costus ; il brûlait ces sept aromates purs, broyés et mêlés en proportions égales.
Et il célébra cette fête pendant sept jours, se réjouissant de tout son cœur et de toute son âme, lui et tous les gens de sa maison, sans qu'aucun étranger ni aucun incirconcis ne fût avec eux.

Et il bénit son Créateur qui l’avait créé, car il reconnut et sut que de lui naîtrait la plantation de vérité pour les générations éternelles, et de lui une postérité sainte, semblable à Celui qui a créé toutes choses.
Et il bénit et se réjouit, et il appela le nom de ce jour de fête : « Fête de réjouissance, agréable au Dieu Très-Haut ».

Et nous le bénîmes pour toujours, ainsi que sa descendance avec lui pour toutes les générations de toute la terre, parce qu’il avait célébré cette fête en son temps, conformément au témoignage des tables célestes.

C’est pourquoi il a été décrété sur les tables célestes au sujet d’Israël qu’il célébrera la fête des Tentes pendant sept jours entiers dans la joie, au septième mois, agréable devant le Seigneur : ordonnance perpétuelle pour leurs générations, d'année en année.

Et cela n’aura point de fin dans le temps, car il a été prescrit à perpétuité à Israël de la célébrer, de demeurer sous des tentes, de poser des couronnes sur leurs têtes, et de prendre des branches touffues et des saules de torrent.

Et Abraham prit de la beauté des palmiers et des fruits d'arbres magnifiques, et tous les jours il faisait le tour de mon autel avec des branches, sept fois le matin, louant et confessant son Dieu en toutes choses dans la joie.
Et la première année de la cinquième semaine de ce jubilé, Isaac fut sevré ; et Abraham fit un grand festin au troisième mois, le jour où son fils Isaac fut sevré.
Et Ismaël, le fils d'Agar, la servante égyptienne, se tenait devant Abraham son père. Et Abraham se réjouit et bénit Dieu parce qu'il vit des fils pour lui et qu'il ne mourut pas sans enfants.

Et il se souvint des paroles qu'il lui avait dites le jour où Loth s'était séparé de lui. Et il se réjouit parce que Dieu lui avait donné une descendance sur la terre pour en hériter, et il bénit de toute sa bouche celui qui a créé l'univers.

Et Sara vit Ismaël qui jouait avec Isaac, et Abraham qui se réjouissait d'une grande joie ; et elle fut jalouse d'Ismaël et dit à Abraham : « Chasse cette servante et son fils, car le fils de cette servante n'héritera pas avec mon fils Isaac. »
Et cette parole parut très mauvaise aux yeux d'Abraham au sujet de la servante et au sujet de son fils, de devoir les chasser loin de lui.
Et Dieu dit à Abraham :
Et il fut troublé et dit : « Me voici. »
Et je lui dis : « Ne porte pas la main sur l'enfant et ne lui fais rien, car maintenant j'ai manifesté que tu crains ton Dieu et que tu ne m'as pas refusé ton fils premier-né. »

Et le prince Mastéma fut confondu. Et levant les yeux, Abraham regarda, et voici qu'un bélier était retenu par ses cornes. Et Abraham alla, prit le bélier et l'offrit en holocauste à la place d'Isaac, son fils.
Et Abraham appela le nom de ce lieu « Le Seigneur a vu », de sorte qu'on dit sur la montagne : « Le Seigneur est apparu » ; c'est le mont Sion.
Et Abraham fut appelé par son nom une seconde fois depuis le ciel, car nous étions là pour lui parler au nom du Seigneur.

Et il dit : « Je le jure par moi-même, dit le Seigneur, puisque tu as accompli cette parole et que tu n'as pas épargné à cause de moi ton fils unique que tu aimais, assurément je te comblerai de bénédictions et je multiplierai ta descendance comme les étoiles du ciel et comme le sable sur le rivage de la mer. Et ta descendance héritera des villes de ses adversaires.
Et toutes les nations de la terre seront bénies en ta descendance, parce que tu as obéi à ma voix ; et j'ai manifesté à tous que tu m'es fidèle en tout ce que je t'ai dit de marcher dans la paix. »
Et Abraham retourna vers ses serviteurs ; et ils se levèrent et partirent pour Beer-Shéba, et Abraham habita près du puits du serment.

Et il célébrait une fête trois fois chaque année. En effet, il célébrait aussi ces sept jours dans la joie, et il l'appela jour de fête du Seigneur d'après les sept jours durant lesquels il était parti et revenu.
Et c'était décrété et écrit sur les tables célestes pour Israël et pour sa descendance, afin qu'ils célèbrent la fête pendant sept jours, se réjouissant dans l'allégresse.
Et la première année de la [première] semaine du quarante-deuxième jubilé, Abraham revint et habita en face d'Hébron, c'est-à-dire Qiriath-Arba, pendant deux semaines d'années.
Et la troisième année de la [première] semaine de ce jubilé, les jours de la vie de Sara s'achevèrent et elle mourut à Hébron.

Et Abraham vint pour la pleurer. Et nous l'éprouvâmes pour voir si son esprit était patient et s'il ne faiblissait pas dans les paroles de sa bouche. Et il fut trouvé très patient en cela aussi, et il ne fut pas troublé.
Car c'est avec longanimité d'esprit qu'il parla avec les fils de Heth, pour qu'ils lui donnent un lieu où ensevelir son mort.

Et Dieu lui accorda sa grâce aux yeux de tous ceux qui le voyaient ; et il adressa sa prière avec douceur aux fils de Heth, et ils lui donnèrent le champ de la caverne double, qui est en face de Mambré, c'est-à-dire Hébron, pour quatre cents deniers.

Et ils le lui demandèrent en disant : « Nous te le donnons gratuitement. » Mais il n'accepta pas gratuitement de leurs mains, car il paya le plein prix du lieu en argent ; et il se prosterna deux fois devant eux, et après cela il ensevelit son mort dans la caverne double.
Et tous les jours de la vie de Sara furent de cent vingt-sept ans, c'est-à-dire deux jubilés et quatre semaines d'années, moins un an : tels sont les jours de la vie de Sara.
Ce fut là la dixième épreuve dans laquelle Abraham fut trouvé fidèle et patient d'esprit.

Et il ne proféra pas de parole de contestation au sujet de la terre, bien que Dieu lui eût promis de la donner à lui et à sa descendance après lui, mais il leur demanda un lieu pour ensevelir son mort. Car il fut trouvé fidèle et fut inscrit comme « ami de Dieu » sur les tables célestes.

Et la quatrième année de cette semaine, Abraham prit une femme pour Isaac, son fils. Et son nom était Rebecca, fille de Betouel, fils de Nahor, frère d'Abraham, sœur de Laban, fille de Betouel ; et Betouel était fils de Milka, femme de Nahor, frère d'Abraham.
Et Abraham prit pour lui une troisième femme, dont le nom était Qetoura, parmi les filles de ses serviteurs nés dans sa maison, car Agar était morte avant Sara.
Et elle lui enfanta six fils : Zimran, Yoqshan, Medan, Madian, Yishbaq et Shouah, en deux semaines d'années.

Et la sixième année de cette deuxième semaine, Rebecca enfanta deux fils à Isaac : Ésaü et Jacob. Et Jacob était doux et droit, et Ésaü était rude, homme des champs et velu ; et Jacob habitait sous des tentes.

Et ils grandirent et devinrent tous deux des jeunes gens. Et Jacob apprit les lettres, mais Ésaü n'apprit pas, car c'était un homme fruste et un chasseur ; mais il apprit la guerre, et toutes ses œuvres étaient rudes.
Et Abraham aimait Jacob, et Isaac aimait Ésaü.

Et Abraham voyait les œuvres d'Ésaü et savait que c'est en Jacob que lui seraient nommés une descendance et un nom ; et il appela Rebecca et lui donna des instructions au sujet de Jacob, car elle aimait Jacob plus qu'Ésaü.
Et il lui dit : « Ma fille, veille sur le nom de mon fils Jacob, car il sera pour moi un mémorial sur la terre, une bénédiction sur les fils des hommes et la gloire de toute ma descendance.
Car je sais que Dieu l'a choisi pour être son peuple saint parmi tous les peuples qui sont sur la surface de toute la terre.
Et voici qu'Isaac aime Ésaü plus que Jacob, mais moi je te vois aimer Jacob en vérité.
Prends encore plus de soin de lui, et que tes yeux soient sur lui avec amour, car il sera pour nous une bénédiction sur la terre, dès maintenant et pour toutes les générations de la terre.

Que tes mains soient donc fortifiées et que ton cœur se réjouisse en ton fils Jacob, car je l'ai aimé plus que tous mes fils. C'est pourquoi lui et sa descendance seront bénis à jamais, et elle remplira toute la terre.
Si un homme pouvait compter le sable de la terre, sa descendance aussi pourrait être comptée.
Et toutes les bénédictions dont Dieu m'a béni, moi et ma descendance, appartiendront à Jacob et à sa descendance pour tous les jours.
Et en sa descendance seront bénis mon nom et le nom de mes pères : Sem, Noé, Hénoch, Mahalaleel, Énosh et Adam.
Et ce sont eux qui poseront les fondements du ciel et affermiront la terre, afin que soient reconnus tous les luminaires du firmament. »
Et Abraham appela
comme ils ont été jugés à cause de leur méchanceté, parce qu'ils se mêlaient aux fornicateurs, pratiquaient l'impureté, commettaient toute abomination et négligeaient les commandements.

Et c'est pourquoi, prenez garde de ne pas livrer votre nom à la malédiction, toute votre vie aux sifflements de mépris, et tous vos fils à l'extermination et à l'épée, et vous seriez maudits comme Sodome et tous vos restes comme les enfants de Gomorrhe.
Et c'est pourquoi je vous adjure, mes fils : aimez le Dieu du ciel et attachez-vous à tous ses commandements, et n'allez pas après toutes leurs abominations et après toutes les impuretés.

Et vous ne vous ferez pas de dieux de fonte ni d'idoles sculptées, car elles sont vaines et il n'y a aucun esprit en elles, puisqu'elles sont l'ouvrage des mains, et tous ceux qui se confient en elles se confient dans le néant. C'est pourquoi ne les servez pas et ne les adorez pas.

Servez plutôt le Dieu Très-Haut et adorez-le en vous prosternant et en attendant sa présence en tout temps ; faites la vérité et la justice devant lui, afin qu'il vous dirige, vous accorde sa miséricorde, fasse descendre pour vous les pluies précoces et tardives, bénisse toutes vos œuvres, tout ce que vous accomplirez sur la terre, et qu'il bénisse ton pain et ton eau, et qu'il bénisse le fruit de tes entrailles et le fruit de ta terre, les troupeaux de tes bœufs et les troupeaux de tes brebis.
Et vous serez en bénédiction sur la terre, et toutes les nations de la terre vous désireront et béniront en mon nom vos fils, afin qu'ils soient en bénédiction tout comme moi. »
Et il donna des présents à Ismaël, à ses fils et aux fils de Qetoura, et il les renvoya loin d'Isaac son fils
et ses fils et les fils de Ketourah et ses fils, et ils habitèrent depuis Faramon jusqu'à l'entrée de Babylone, dans tout le pays oriental, sur la face du désert.
Et ceux-ci se mélangèrent à ceux-là, et leur nom s'attacha aux Arabes et aux Ismaélites jusqu'à ce jour.

Et la sixième année des semaines de ce septième jubilé, Abraham appela son fils Isaac et lui donna des instructions, disant : « Je suis devenu vieux et je ne connais pas le jour de ma mort, et je suis rassasié de mes jours.

Et voici, mon fils, que je suis âgé de cent soixante-quinze ans ; durant les jours de ma vie, j'ai toujours gardé la mémoire de notre Dieu et je l'ai cherché de toute ma force, afin de faire toute sa volonté et de marcher droit dans toutes ses voies.
Et c'est pourquoi mon âme a haï les idoles et j'ai méprisé ceux qui les servent. Et j'ai appliqué mon cœur et mon esprit à garder et à faire la volonté de celui qui m'a créé.

Car Dieu est vivant, saint, fidèle et juste ; et il n'y a auprès de lui aucune acception de personnes pour recevoir des présents, car Dieu est juste et exerce le jugement sur tous ceux qui transgressent ses paroles et qui méprisent son témoignage.
Et toi, mon fils, garde ses préceptes, ses commandements et ses jugements, et ne va pas après les abominations ni après les idoles de métal fondu.
Et ne mangez aucun sang d'aucune chair, qu'il s'agisse de ce qui est sur la terre ou de ce qui vole dans les airs.

Et si tu immoles une victime de sacrifices pacifiques, vous l'immolerez et vous répandrez son sang sur l'autel. Et tu offriras tout le sang de l'holocauste sur l'autel, avec de la fleur de farine pétrie à l'huile et avec sa libation de vin, tu offriras toutes ces choses sur l'autel des sacrifices : c'est une odeur agréable devant Dieu.

Et tu offriras la graisse du sacrifice d'action de grâces sur le feu, sur l'autel : la graisse qui recouvre les entrailles et toute la graisse qui est sur les intestins, et les deux rognons avec toute la graisse qui est dessus et celle qui est sur les flancs, et tu sépareras le lobe du foie avec les rognons.
Et ainsi tu offriras le tout comme une odeur agréable, agréée en présence du Seigneur, avec leurs offrandes et avec son vin, comme une odeur agréable, pain des sacrifices pour le Seigneur.
Et vous mangerez la chair ce jour-là et le lendemain, et le soleil ne se couchera pas
les richesses d'Isaac étaient nombreuses à Beershéba ; et Isaac partait et inspectait encore ce qu'il possédait, puis il retourna auprès de son père.
En ce temps-là, Ismaël vint voir son père et ils se réunirent tous deux ensemble. Et Isaac immola un sacrifice et l'offrit sur l'autel de son père qu'il avait bâti à Hébron.

Et il fit un sacrifice de communion et prépara un festin de joie en présence d'Ismaël son frère. Et Rebecca prépara une galette nouvelle avec du blé nouveau et la donna à Jacob son fils, pour qu'il l'apporte à son père Abraham parmi les prémices de la terre, afin qu'il mange et bénisse le Créateur de toutes choses avant de mourir.
Et Isaac envoya aussi par les mains de Jacob les meilleures parts de ses sacrifices de communion et du vin à son père Abraham, afin qu'il mange et qu'il boive.

Et Abraham mangea et but, et il bénit le Seigneur Très-Haut qui a créé le ciel et la terre, qui a produit toute la graisse de la terre et l'a donnée aux fils des hommes pour qu'ils mangent, boivent et bénissent leur Créateur.

Et maintenant, je te rends grâce, mon Dieu, parce que tu m'as fait voir ce jour ; et voici que je suis âgé de cent soixante-quinze ans, vieillard rassasié de jours, et tous mes jours ont été pour moi des jours de paix.
Et l'épée de l'ennemi n'a pas dominé sur moi durant tous les jours où tu m'as donné ceux-ci pour être mes fils, tous les jours de ma vie jusqu'à ce jour.

Que ta miséricorde et ta paix soient maintenant sur cet enfant, Seigneur, et sur sa postérité, afin qu'ils soient pour toi un peuple agréable et un héritage parmi tous les fils de la terre, dès maintenant et pour tous les jours des générations de la terre, pour tous les siècles.

Et Abraham appela Jacob son fils et dit : « Mon fils Jacob, que le Dieu de toutes choses te bénisse et te fortifie pour faire la vérité et sa volonté devant lui, et pour choisir d'être pour lui, toi et ta descendance, un peuple selon sa volonté en tous les jours. Et toi, mon fils Jacob, approche-toi de moi et embrasse-moi. »

Et Jacob s'approcha et l'embrassa. Et il dit : « Béni soit mon fils Jacob et tous ses fils devant le Dieu Très-Haut en toutes choses ! Que Dieu te donne une descendance de vérité, et parmi tes fils il y aura sanctification au milieu de toute la terre ! Les nations te serviront et tous les peuples se prosterneront devant ton nom !
Deviens fort devant les hommes et exerce le pouvoir sur toute la descendance de Seth. Alors tes voies et les voies de tes fils seront justifiées, afin qu'ils deviennent un peuple saint.

Que le Dieu Très-Haut te donne toutes les bénédictions dont il m'a béni, et dont il a béni Noé et Adam, et qu'elles reposent sur le sommet de la sanctification de ta descendance de génération en génération, pour l'éternité !
Et il te purifiera de toute souillure et de toute injustice, pour faire grâce à toutes tes iniquités et à tes négligences ; il te fortifiera, te bénira, et tu hériteras de toute la terre.

Et il renouvellera son alliance avec toi, afin que tu sois pour lui un peuple d'héritage pour tous les siècles, et lui sera pour toi et pour ta descendance un Dieu en vérité et en justice tous les jours de la terre.

Et toi, mon fils Jacob, souviens-toi de mes paroles et garde les préceptes de ton père Abraham. Sépare-toi des nations et ne mange point avec elles, n'agis point selon leurs œuvres et ne deviens point leur compagnon, car leurs œuvres sont souillure et toutes leurs voies sont impureté, abomination et infamie.
Car ils sacrifient aux morts et adorent les démons, ils mangent sur les tombeaux et toutes leurs œuvres sont vaines et de nulle valeur.

Et ils n'ont pas de cœur pour réfléchir, et leurs yeux ne voient pas ce que sont leurs œuvres ni comment ils s'égarent, disant au bois : « Tu es mon dieu », et à la pierre : « Tu es mon seigneur et mon libérateur » ; et ils n'ont point de cœur.
Et toi, mon fils Jacob, le Dieu Très-Haut t'aidera et le Dieu d'Adam te fortifiera, et il te séparera de toutes leurs abominations et de toute erreur
dans sa cent soixante-quinzième année, il acheva les jours de sa vie, vieillard et rassasié de jours.

C'est pourquoi les jours des anciens formaient sa vie. Et au dix-neuvième jubilé après le déluge, les jours de ces jubilés commencèrent à diminuer, les hommes vieillirent plus vite et les jours de leur vie diminuèrent à cause de la tribulation causée par beaucoup et parce qu'ils devinrent mauvais dans leurs voies, à l'exception d'Abraham.

Car Abraham était parfait dans toutes ses œuvres avec Dieu, et agréable dans la vérité tous les jours de sa vie. Et voici qu'il n'accomplit pas quatre jubilés dans sa vie avant de vieillir à cause des méchants, et il fut rassasié de ses jours.
Et les générations qui s'élèveront depuis lors jusqu'au jour du grand jugement vieilliront rapidement, avant d'avoir accompli deux jubilés, et l'esprit de leur intelligence passera loin d'elles.

Et en ces jours-là, si un homme vit un jubilé et demi d'années, on dira de lui : « Sa vie a été longue ! » Et la plus grande partie de ses jours [ne sera que peine] et angoisse, et il n'y a point de paix.

Car il y aura plaie sur plaie, douleur sur douleur, tribulation sur tribulation, mauvais bruit sur mauvais bruit, infirmité sur infirmité, et tous ses jugements mauvais selon cela même, avec corruption, désastres, neiges, gelées, glace, fièvre, froids, étouffement, famine, mort, épée, captivité et tous les fléaux de lamentation.
Et toutes ces choses surviendront sur la génération inique, qui commet l'iniquité sur la terre avec impureté, fornications, souillures et les abominations de leurs œuvres.

Alors ils diront : « Les jours d'autrefois étaient nombreux, jusqu'à mille ans, et étaient de bons jours. Mais voici que les jours de notre vie, si l'homme vit beaucoup, sont de soixante-dix ans, et s'il est fort, de quatre-vingts ans ; et ceux-ci sont mauvais, et il n'y a aucune paix dans les jours de cette très mauvaise génération. »

Et dans cette même génération, les enfants reprendront leurs pères et leurs anciens à cause de l'iniquité et des injustices, et à cause de la parole de leur bouche, et à cause des grandes méchancetés qu'ils commettent parce qu'ils abandonnent l'alliance que Dieu a conclue entre lui et eux, afin de garder et d'accomplir tous ses commandements, ses préceptes et toutes ses lois, sans que nul ne s'en écarte ni à droite ni à gauche.
C'est pourquoi tous sont devenus mauvais, toute bouche profère le mal, toutes leurs actions sont impureté et haine, et toutes leurs voies sont souillures, abomination et destruction.

Et voici que la terre périra à cause de toutes leurs œuvres, et il n'y aura plus de semence, ni de vin, ni d'huile, parce que toutes leurs œuvres sont devenues mauvaises ; et tous périssent — bêtes sauvages, bétail, oiseaux et tous les poissons de la mer — à cause de la méchanceté des fils des hommes.

Et ils se querelleront les uns avec les autres : les jeunes avec les vieillards et les vieillards avec les jeunes, le pauvre avec le riche, le petit avec le grand et l'indigent avec celui qui exerce le pouvoir, au sujet de la loi et de l'alliance, car ils ont oublié le commandement, l'alliance, les jours de fête, le mois, le sabbat, le jubilé et tous les jugements.
Et ils se dresseront avec l'arc, l'épée et la guerre pour les ramener dans la voie, mais ils ne reviendront pas, jusqu'à ce que beaucoup de sang soit versé sur la terre, les uns par les autres.

Et ceux qui ont été préservés sur la voie de la vérité ne s'éloigneront pas de leur malice et ne se convertiront pas ; car tous s'enorgueilliront pour la fraude et pour les richesses, afin que chacun s'empare de tout ce qui appartient à son prochain ; et ils invoqueront un grand nom, mais non en vérité ni en justice, et ils profaneront le saint sanctuaire par des abominations d'iniquité et des impuretés.
Et il y aura une grande colère du Seigneur contre les œuvres de cette génération ; et il leur enverra l'épée et le jugement pour la captivité, le pillage et la dévoration.
Et il suscitera contre eux des pécheurs, les pécheurs des nations, pour lesquels il n'y a pas
ans. Et Abimélek donna des ordres à son sujet, disant : « Tout homme qui lui causera du tort ou touchera à quelque chose qui lui appartient sera puni de mort. »
Et Isaac grandit dans le pays des Philistins, et il acquit de grands biens : des bœufs, des brebis, des chameaux, des ânes et une nombreuse suite de serviteurs.
Et il sema dans le pays des Philistins et récolta au centuple ; Isaac devint extrêmement puissant, et les Philistins furent jaloux de lui.
Et tous les puits que les serviteurs d'Abraham avaient creusés du vivant d'Abraham, les Philistins les bouchèrent après la mort d'Abraham et les remplirent de terre.
Et Abimélek dit à Isaac : « Éloigne-toi de nous, car tu es devenu beaucoup plus puissant que nous. » Et Isaac partit de là avec les siens, la première année de la septième semaine.

Et s’en retournant de là, ils creusèrent les puits d’eau qu’avaient creusés les serviteurs de son père Abraham et que les Philistins avaient comblés après la mort d’Abraham son père ; et il leur donna des noms d’après les noms que son père leur avait donnés.

Et les serviteurs d’Isaac creusèrent des puits dans le torrent et y trouvèrent de l’eau vive, et les bergers de Gérar se querellèrent avec les bergers d’Isaac, en disant : « L’eau est à nous. » Et Isaac appela le puits du nom de « Difficulté », parce qu’ils avaient été difficiles avec nous.

Et ils creusèrent un autre puits et se querellèrent aussi à son sujet, et il l’appela du nom d’« Inimitiés ». Et ils creusèrent un troisième puits et ne se querellèrent pas pour lui, et il l’appela du nom d’« Espace au large ». Et Isaac dit : « Car maintenant le Seigneur Dieu nous a mis au large et nous a multipliés sur la terre. »
Et la première année de la première semaine.

Le Seigneur lui apparut cette nuit-là, le premier jour du premier mois, et lui dit : « Je suis le Dieu d’Abraham ton père. Ne crains pas, car je suis avec toi, et je te bénirai et je multiplierai ta descendance comme le sable de la terre à cause d’Abraham mon serviteur. »
Et il bâtit qu’avait bâti son père, et il invoqua le nom du Seigneur et immola des victimes au Dieu d’Abraham son père.
Et ils creusèrent un puits et trouvèrent de l’eau vive.

Et les serviteurs d’Isaac creusèrent de nouveau un autre puits et ne trouvèrent pas d’eau ; ils vinrent et annoncèrent à Isaac qu’ils n’avaient pas trouvé d’eau. Et Isaac dit : « C'est parce que j’ai prêté serment ce jour-là aux Philistins que cette parole nous est arrivée. »
Et il appela ce lieu du nom de « Puits du serment », car c’est là qu’avaient juré Abimélek, Ochozias son compagnon et Pikhol le chef de son armée.
Et Isaac reconnut en ce jour-là que il avait juré de faire la paix avec lui.

Et Isaac maudit les Philistins en ce jour-là et dit : « Maudit soit le Philistin au jour de la colère et de l’indignation du milieu de toutes les nations ! Que Dieu le livre à l’opprobre, à la malédiction et à l’indignation de la colère, entre les mains d’un peuple pécheur et entre les mains des Kittim !
Et qu’un peuple juste l’extirpe par le jugement de dessous le ciel ! Car ils sont ennemis et adversaires de mes fils tout au long de leurs générations sur la terre.

Et il ne leur sera laissé aucun reste ni rescapé au jour de la colère du jugement, mais ils seront voués à la perdition et à l’extermination, afin que toute la race des Philistins soit ôtée de la surface de la terre et qu’il ne leur reste aucun nom sur la terre.

Et s’il monte jusqu’au ciel, il en sera précipité ; et là où il fuira, il en sera arraché ; et s’il se cache au milieu des nations, il sera extirpé ; et s’il descend dans le séjour des morts, là son jugement sera abondant et il n’y aura là aucune paix pour lui.

Et s’il s’en va en captivité entre les mains de tous ceux qui en veulent à sa vie, il périra aussi au milieu du séjour des morts, et il n’aura ni descendance ni nom sur toute la terre, car il s’en ira dans une malédiction éternelle.
Car il est ainsi écrit et consigné contre lui sur les tables célestes, pour qu’il lui soit fait au jour du jugement, afin qu’il soit extirpé de la surface de la terre. »
Et la deuxième année des semaines de ce jubilé, Rebecca appela son fils Jacob et lui parla en disant : « Mon fils, ne prends pas pour toi »
de son dessein, et il s’indignera contre moi, et j’attirerai sur moi une malédiction et non une bénédiction.
Et Rebecca sa mère lui dit : « Que ta malédiction retombe sur moi, mon fils ! Écoute seulement ma voix. »
Et Jacob écouta la voix de sa mère Rebecca ; il s’en alla, prit deux chevreaux de chèvres tendres et bons, et les apporta à sa mère, et sa mère en fit un plat comme il l’aimait.

Et Rebecca prit les meilleurs vêtements d’Ésaü, son fils aîné, qui étaient avec elle dans la maison, et en vêtit Jacob, son fils cadet, et elle mit les peaux des chevreaux sur ses bras, sur ses épaules et sur la nudité de son cou.
Elle remit les mets qu’elle avait préparés et le pain entre les mains de Jacob son fils.
Et Jacob entra auprès de son père et dit : « Je suis ton fils ; j’ai fait comme tu me l’as dit. Lève-toi, assieds-toi et mange de mon gibier, mon père, afin que ton âme me bénisse. »
Et Isaac dit à son fils : « Comment as-tu trouvé si vite, mon fils ? »
Et Jacob dit : « Parce que le Seigneur ton Dieu l’a fait venir au-devant de moi. »
Et Isaac lui dit : « Approche-toi de moi, et je te palperai, mon fils, pour savoir si tu es mon fils Ésaü. »
Et Jacob s’approcha d’Isaac son père, et il le palpa et dit : « La voix est certes la voix de Jacob, mais les mains sont les mains d’Ésaü. »
Et il ne le reconnut pas, car c’était un dessein venu du ciel pour détourner son esprit ; et il ne reconnut pas que ses mains étaient velues comme les mains d’Ésaü son frère. Et il le bénit.
